codeReview.summary: The commit correctly removes `/dashboard-legacy`, switches embed/serving to `ui/dist`, and deletes the legacy `src/pages/*.js`/router/store/client surfaces. However, legacy root UI artifacts were left behind, so the feature does not fully satisfy the stated removal scope.

issues.description: Legacy entrypoint `app.js` still exists and imports `./src/main.js`, which was deleted in this feature. The feature description explicitly requires deleting legacy-only dashboard files; leaving this broken legacy file means the legacy surface cleanup is incomplete.

The legacy global stylesheet remains in-repo (`styles.css`, 2k+ lines) even though the feature scope called out cleaning up old `styles.css` after Tailwind migration. This is another leftover legacy artifact not removed by the cutover.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The fullstack-worker skill enforces test-first sequencing, but this deletion-heavy migration required implementation-first then test realignment; worker marked `followedProcedure=false` with a justified deviation. Skill procedure likely needs an explicit exception path for large cutover/removal features.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Handoff skillFeedback in mission handoff file (`...react-remove-legacy__1db7d178-89b5-4a31-9e03-7f3c0ba22e9f.json`) shows deviation at step '2. Write Tests First — Both Layers' with rationale.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Service command catalog still includes a Playwright command targeting a removed `.spec.js` file.

summary: Feature is close but not fully complete: runtime route/embed cutover is correct, yet legacy root files (`ui/app.js`, `ui/styles.css`) remain despite explicit removal scope. Marked fail pending cleanup of those remaining legacy artifacts.
